full_judgment:
2. The suit is one for declaration of title to 2.33 acres of land recorded in C.S. Plot No. 9 and 10 of Khatian No. 4 fully described in the schedule to the plaint. The case of the plaintiffs is briefly this: One Salimuddin had raiyati interest in the disputed plots. Majitullah, the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs had Korfa interest under Salimuddin. The raiyati of Salimuddin was auction sold for arrears of rent in 1934. Mobarak, the predecessor-in-interest of the defendants, auction purchased the holding. He did not annual the Korfa interest of Majitullah but recognised him as a tenant. In the M.R.R. Khatian the suit plots had, however, been wrongly recorded in the name of the defendants. 

 3. Defendant No. 1 (Respondent No.1) contested the suit. His defence on the other hand, is that Majitullah surrendered his Korfa interest in favour of Salimuddin and continued to possess the land as bargadar under him executing registered kabuliyats. The interest of Mobarak who auction-purchased the holding devolved upon the defendants by way of inheritance. Mobarak sold 1.68 acres to Miazan, one of sons of Salimuddin. Accordingly their names were correctly recorded in the M.R.R. Khatian. The defendants have had been in possession of the disputed lands and the plaintiffs have no right, title or interest therein. 

 9. it is no doubt true that an entry in the C.S. Khatian must be presumed to be correct unless the contrary is proved, but when the matter is investigated by the Court on the evidence adduced by the parties on the point in controversy, the entry loses its significance. In the instant case, the lower appellate court, after a detailed discussion of the evidence of the parties came to the conclusion that after the auction sale of the raiyat interest of Salimuddin in 1939 there had been a change in the status and possession of the parties. Therefore the presumption of right, title and possession on the basis of C.S. Khatian did not hold good any more.
